scope: Isolated rehearsals only. No shared installation, credential or database was touched.
meaning: A rehearsal that did not run is not evidence that the fault is handled. This file records what was exercised, not what was hoped.

items.establishes: The API process stops and starts again with retained cases, releases and private bytes intact.
items.reason: No process-level restart harness exists. The workload harness restarts a worker, not the API server, and restarting a shared API is out of scope for an isolated rehearsal.

items.establishes: A worker disappears mid-job and its work is recovered by another worker without double publication.
items.reason: No worker-kill harness exists. Expired-lease recovery is covered by stale-lease; killing a live worker is a different fault and is not exercised.

items.establishes: An expired delivery lease is recovered and a cancelled job cannot publish.
Private object bytes survive a paired database+object restore with matching hashes.
A provider outage produces durable backoff and a resumable checkpoint rather than a lost request.
An exhausted shared quota refuses new billable work and records the uncertain charge conservatively.
A storage reservation refuses work beyond the declared budget instead of failing after publication.
A lost provider response retains the original request identity instead of creating a duplicate.
A revoked source stops retrieval and its retained evidence stops being served under the old grant.
An interrupted expiry deletion retries and leaves an authorized tombstone rather than a resurrection.
A paired database+object restore retains cases, approval, jobs and private bytes.
A nominated rollback binary is provisioned, migrated forward and recovered without losing cases or dependencies.
items.reason: Run scripts/ops/qualify_rollback.py with a nominated --binary and --manifest. A source archive is not an installed rollback binary.
